claims.text: The initial material is as-cast equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr.
As-cast equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr has 8–16% room-temperature tensile ductility.
As-cast equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr has a yield strength of 163–530 MPa at 1000 °C.
Untreated as-cast HfNbTaTiZr undergoes rapid oxidation at high temperatures.
Pack cementation at approximately 950 °C for 6 hours using about 20 wt.% Al, 3 wt.% activator, and balance Al2O3 will aluminize the alloy surface.
The pack cementation treatment will drive aluminum diffusion into the surface of HfNbTaTiZr.
Aluminum diffusion will produce an in situ aluminide surface layer.
High-temperature exposure in an oxidizing atmosphere will convert the aluminide surface into a continuous, adherent, slowly growing Al2O3 scale.
The Al2O3 scale will impede oxygen ingress into the alloy.
Aluminized HfNbTaTiZr will have significantly better oxidation resistance than untreated cast HfNbTaTiZr at 1000 °C.
The surface treatment will not materially alter the bulk microstructure responsible for the alloy's mechanical performance.
Aluminizing will have minimal impact on the alloy's high-temperature yield strength.
Aluminizing will have minimal impact on the alloy's room-temperature tensile ductility.
The proposed performance boundary is approximately 1000 °C in air or controlled oxygen under strain rates of 10^-4–10^-2 s^-1.
Protective alumina scales produced by aluminizing are effective on other high-temperature alloys.
